newsitem.title: THAILAND: Karens urge UNHCR to run refugee camps in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Karens urge UNHCR to run refugee camps in Thailand.

text.p: Karen refugees on Thursday appealed to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to start administering ethnic Karen camps in Thailand.

The call was made by the Karen Refugee Committee (KRC), an affiliate of the Karen National Union (KNU) guerrilla group, which has administered the refugee shelters near Thailand's western border with Burma since 1984.
But the Thai army said it would not allow the UNHCR to run the camps.
"These people are not refugees. They are displaced persons who fled from fighting and are seeking temporary refuge. We have been giving them humanitarian aid," an army spokesman told Reuters.
Over 90,000 Karen refugees, mostly family members of KNU followers who fled attacks by Burmese troops inside Burma, live in the sprawling camps.
Last month the Thai government changed its policy and announced plans to establish more law and order in the camps and said it would deploy soldiers there.
The KRC said the refugees were living in fear because Burmese troops had launched an offensive against KNU guerrillas and deployed their troops close to the refugee camps.
They were also regularly harrassed by the DKBA, a breakaway Bhuddhist faction from the Christian-dominated KNU, it said.

"The situation being as such we, the KRC, would like to request the Thai government to permit the UNHCR to perform its mandated role in protecting refugees rights and security and to continue to extend refuge...in the border area of Thailand," the KRC said in a statement obtained by Reuters on Thursday.
The UNHCR provides some assistance to the refugees but Thailand is reluctant to give it a total mandate to look after the refugees.
